items.context: Two reference patterns already exist in the codebase. `handleCustomerUpdated()` (stripe_webhook_service.go:587-712) and `addCredits()` (stripe_credit_service.go:140-214) use raw `s.db.Begin()` with `defer tx.Rollback()` and explicit `tx.Commit()`. A newer canonical helper `WithTransaction(ctx, db, opts, func(tx *sql.Tx) error)` exists at dbhelpers.go:210-259 and centralises rollback/panic handling. Which should the fix use?

options.label: Use the WithTransaction helper
options.rationale: Centralised rollback + panic safety, less boilerplate, and aligns with the 'canonical helper' direction. Slightly different shape from handleCustomerUpdated but the helper is the go-forward pattern.

options.label: Use raw s.db.Begin() / defer Rollback / Commit like handleCustomerUpdated
options.rationale: Matches the closest sibling pattern in the same file; lower cognitive overhead for reviewers familiar with that function.

items.context: `handleCheckoutCompleted()` branches into three paths after the shared `UPDATE checkout_sessions` at lines 191-197: credit-topup (already atomic inside `addCredits`), supporter, and subscription. The subscription branch calls `handleSubscriptionCompletion` (INSERT into subscriptions) and then `createSubscriptionSchedule` (INSERT into subscription_schedules for scheduled-downgrade plans). The research finding (#6) names only the checkout_sessions+subscription pair. Where should the transaction boundary land?

options.label: Wrap UPDATE checkout_sessions + INSERT subscriptions + INSERT subscription_schedules (when applicable) in one tx
options.rationale: Strongest atomicity: a failed schedule insert also rolls back the subscription, preventing a user with an active subscription but a missing scheduled-downgrade. Matches the 'either both succeed or both roll back' intent broadly.

options.label: Wrap only UPDATE checkout_sessions + INSERT subscriptions; leave createSubscriptionSchedule outside
options.rationale: Narrowest interpretation of the research finding. Smaller blast radius; if schedule insert fails, the user still gets an active subscription (they'd just miss the scheduled downgrade).

options.label: Extend to all branches (subscription + credit topup + supporter) — refactor each branch to pass a tx through
options.rationale: Maximises consistency but requires refactoring `addCredits` and the supporter flow, widening scope beyond this fix item.

items.topic: How to inject failure in the atomicity test
items.context: The key new test (`TestHandleCheckoutCompleted_SubscriptionInsertFailure_RollsBackStatus`) must deterministically force the subscription INSERT to fail after the checkout_sessions UPDATE has run inside the tx, then assert no state leaked. Stable test mechanics matter — a flaky failure-injection test is worse than no test.

options.label: Pre-seed an incompatible subscriptions row so the INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE fails via a schema constraint (e.g., NOT NULL mismatch through a plan-option with empty required fields)
options.rationale: Deterministic, uses real DB. No new seam in production code. Easiest to reason about.

options.label: Introduce a test-only seam (e.g., a `subscriptionInsertHook` on StripeService) that returns an error when set
options.rationale: Clean test isolation but adds a production-code seam purely for test use; contradicts seam-discovery-and-enforcement guidance unless the seam has dual value.

options.label: Use sqlmock against an in-memory DB instead of testcontainers
options.rationale: Fastest tests but diverges from the existing integration-test pattern; per project memory, mocks in DB tests have burned us before (LPBS prefers real DB via testcontainers).

items.topic: Location of the shared UPDATE checkout_sessions statement after refactor
items.context: Today the `UPDATE checkout_sessions SET status='complete', subscription_id=..., ...` at lines 191-197 runs BEFORE the branch split, using one SQL for all three branches (credit-topup, supporter, subscription). If only the subscription branch moves into a tx, we need to decide where this shared UPDATE lives so the other branches keep working correctly.

options.label: Move the UPDATE into each branch; the subscription branch runs it inside the tx, credit-topup and supporter run it as bare db.Exec after their own work
options.rationale: Clearest ownership per branch; each branch's writes are co-located. Slight duplication of the SET clause across branches, offset by explicit per-branch semantics.

options.label: Keep the UPDATE shared and pre-branch; the subscription branch then runs its INSERT in its own tx (accepting that the UPDATE is outside the tx — preserving today's gap)
options.rationale: Minimal refactor but does NOT close the atomicity gap — explicitly rejected by the item description.

options.label: Extract a helper `updateCheckoutSessionComplete(tx_or_db, ...)` that each branch calls, passing either `tx` or `s.db`
options.rationale: DRY; one SQL source of truth. Adds a tiny helper but makes scope changes easier later. Requires an Execer-like interface or two overloads.

items.text: The research finding refers to the function as `insertOrUpdateSubscription()`, but the actual symbol in stripe_webhook_service.go:230 is `handleSubscriptionCompletion()`. The implementation will target the real name; no rename needed.

The pre-branch short-circuit at stripe_webhook_service.go:184-189 (`if session.Status == "complete" { return nil }`) is load-bearing: it makes Stripe's retries no-ops when the previous attempt succeeded. The fix preserves it. It does NOT protect against concurrent duplicate webhook deliveries (two Stripe events in flight), but that race is explicitly covered by the initiative's Action 2 (reconciliation ticker) and Action 3 (payment anomaly log) — out of scope here.

On retry after a rolled-back failure, both the checkout_sessions UPDATE and the subscriptions INSERT are natively idempotent via `ON CONFLICT (session_id) DO UPDATE` and `ON CONFLICT (subscription_id) DO UPDATE` respectively. No new idempotency column is needed for this fix — a broader `stripe_event_id` idempotency layer is in Action 3's scope.

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md scaffold with all 13 mandatory sections populated from code investigation, research conclusions, and the desktop-monetization-assurance initiative context. Contract Decisions and Non-goals sections explicitly commit to WithTransaction helper and narrow (subscription-branch only) scope; these can be overridden by the d1/d2 selections in this round. Testing Plan enumerates 4 new/extended tests covering failure rollback, schedule-failure rollback, happy-path, and retry-after-rollback.
